name: Lemon Squeezy
heading: Lemon Squeezy reviews
intro: Lemon Squeezy sits at 1.2 out of 5 on Trustpilot across 173 reviews, while Product Hunt has it at 4.8 from 76. Both are accurate about different people. Product Hunt collects founders reviewing the product itself, mostly before the Stripe acquisition. Most Trustpilot reviews since 2025 come from sellers who never got past onboarding or never got paid. G2 lists the product with zero reviews and Capterra has no listing at all.

seo.metaTitle: Lemon Squeezy Reviews: 1.2 Stars and Held Payouts
seo.metaDescription: Lemon Squeezy rates 1.2 out of 5 across 173 Trustpilot reviews, dominated by rejected applications and pending payouts, against 4.8 on Product Hunt.

faqs.question: Are these Lemon Squeezy reviews verified?
faqs.answer: The figures on this page come from Trustpilot, Product Hunt and G2 and were current in August 2026. Trustpilot is an open platform, so anyone can post, and its Lemon Squeezy page skews heavily toward people whose store application was rejected, which is worth knowing before you weigh a 1.2. Product Hunt reviews are attached to accounts and run from the 2021 launch to the present month. G2 verifies reviewers before publishing and has none for this product, while Capterra has no Lemon Squeezy listing at all. None of these are reviews submitted to this site, and no merchant has published one here yet, which is why the list above is empty rather than showing a borrowed rating.

faqs.question: Why is Lemon Squeezy rated 1.2 on Trustpilot but 4.8 on Product Hunt?
faqs.answer: The two pages cover different people. Product Hunt collected its 76 reviews across 51 launches starting in 2021, from founders who had a working store and were describing the product. Its own page summary notes that the more recent feedback there is sharply negative. Trustpilot's 173 reviews are dominated by 2025 and 2026, and most of them are not about the product at all. They are about an application rejected after document collection, a verification that ran for weeks, or a payout that stayed pending. Someone who never got an account never rates the checkout. The Trustpilot score measures the front door and the Product Hunt score measures the house.

faqs.question: What do Lemon Squeezy reviewers complain about most?
faqs.answer: Onboarding, by a wide margin. Reviewers describe submitting passports, company documents and personal social media accounts, waiting one to four weeks, then being rejected in a sentence that gives no reason and offers no appeal. Several were selling exactly the software and ebooks the published policy lists as acceptable. Second is payouts: money sitting pending for weeks or months, and in some cases payout cycles failing repeatedly with no notification. Third, running underneath both, is support. There is no phone number, tickets and emails go days or weeks without a reply, and the CEO acknowledged slower support responses in a post dated 28 January 2026.

faqs.question: Is Lemon Squeezy still accepting new sellers?
faqs.answer: Yes. Registration is open, and the volume of 2026 reviews from people who applied confirms applications are still being processed, whatever the outcome. What has changed is what happens next. The signup flow now opens on a step headed Tell us about your business that says the answers will be used to recommend the best path for your business, and Stripe, which acquired Lemon Squeezy in July 2024, has its own merchant of record product in Stripe Managed Payments. In January 2026 the CEO wrote that the goal is to give Lemon Squeezy users an easy way to migrate to it. No end date has been published for the Lemon Squeezy platform, and the changelog has had no entry since 18 August 2025.

blocks.html:
What the third-party review record shows

As of August 2026 Lemon Squeezy carries 1.2 out of 5 on Trustpilot from 173 reviews. Product Hunt carries 4.8 out of 5 from 76. G2 lists the product and shows zero reviews under a line saying it has not been reviewed yet, and Capterra has no Lemon Squeezy listing to look up at all.

Split by who is writing, the two scores stop contradicting each other. The Product Hunt reviews are founder write-ups of the product itself, and those founders describe it removing work they would otherwise have had to build, such as license key issuing and tax handling. Of the 173 Trustpilot reviews, 128 were posted in 2025 or 2026, and those have a different subject. Not people describing the product, but people describing an application that was rejected, a verification that never finished, or a payout that never arrived.

So this is a review record about onboarding and support rather than about features, and it matches what the company has said about itself. In a post dated 28 January 2026 the CEO wrote that the acquisition had meant slower support responses and less frequent product updates. The public changelog has had no entry since 18 August 2025.

blocks.title: Themes across public reviews
pros: Founders on Product Hunt describe the merchant of record model removing the VAT and sales tax work they would otherwise have had to build or outsource

License key issuing and management is the feature reviewers name as the reason they chose it over a plain checkout, including a founder on Product Hunt who weighed Gumroad and raw Stripe and said it handled licensing so he never had to build it
Setup is repeatedly described as fast, with reviewers reporting a store and a working checkout inside a day
Sellers in regions with limited payout options say Lemon Squeezy was the platform they could switch to, one crediting its support for virtual bank accounts like Wise
One five-star seller reports collecting over $65,000 in new customers in the first three months and credits the click-through rate on Lemon Squeezy checkouts for it
Five-star reviews from 2023 describe support as fast and helpful, which is the opposite of what the 2025 and 2026 reviews report
cons: Store applications rejected after KYC and KYB document collection with no stated reason is the single most repeated complaint, running through 2025 and 2026
Verification is described as taking one to four weeks against an advertised one to three business days, with one reviewer reporting a two month identity review
Payouts stuck in pending for weeks or months recur across reviews, including from sellers who say nobody told them a payout cycle had failed
Support is email and ticket only with no phone line, and reviewers on both platforms report waits of days to weeks or no reply at all
Rejections are reported for products the published policy allows, including desktop software and ebooks, with no appeal route offered
There is no self-serve account deletion, and reviewers say they had to contact support to get an account removed

blocks.html:
What the review record will not tell you

A share of the one-star reviews are complaints about the merchant of record model rather than about this company. An MoR is the legal seller, which means it underwrites you, and underwriting means saying no to people. Every MoR runs the same KYC and KYB gate and every one of them refuses applications. If you want an account you can open in ten minutes, what you want is a gateway plus your own tax registrations. The 13 day hold and the twice monthly payout calendar belong in the same bucket: they are how the model carries refund and chargeback exposure on your behalf, and a reviewer who arrived expecting next-day funding will rate that as a defect. It is the trade.

Strip those out and what remains is specific to Lemon Squeezy, and it is the silence. Applications sitting for weeks with no decision. Payout cycles failing without anyone being told. Tickets going unanswered. That is a staffing and ownership problem rather than a model problem, and the CEO's own January 2026 note about slower support responses corroborates it rather than answering it.

The practical move is to get through approval before you build anything, and to keep a second route open while you do. Paddle publishes the same 5% + 50 cent headline and runs its own underwriting, and Polar is the newer merchant of record that indie software sellers weigh against it. If your business sits inside the 38 locations Stripe Managed Payments accepts sellers from, Stripe is where Lemon Squeezy's own team has said the product is heading.

quotesNote: Six excerpts from Lemon Squeezy's Trustpilot page, which sits at 1.2 out of 5 and is dominated by sellers rejected at onboarding or left unpaid, so it captures the unhappy end of the record rather than the merchants quietly running stores.

quotes.text: I made numerous software sales through Lemon Squeezy, and never received a single payout. They do not respond to emails, "support tickets" and do not have a phone number.
Store application rejected after KYC/KYB submission with zero explanation.
Waited ten days. Received a rejection explaining that they don't support "gaming currencies" and wishing me luck in "the gaming space". I have never sold a game or anything game-adjacent.
Spent over 2 weeks waiting to get approved. Was asked to provide information that I've already provided. Was denied with zero indication as to why.
It took a full month just to get my account approved. After that I used them for 6 months and the experience was terrible from start to finish.
For me, it has been a 2 month wait (compared to their advertised 1 - 3 business day wait) with no contact from them despite numerous emails and chats with their help bot.
